commits.title: The store's menu sends each address once

changes.how: storeTabs() (about line 432) gives every tab an 'also' list that repeats every address of the section, and storeAreas() (about line 451) sends the same addresses again as 'prefixes' and a third time as each item's href. Stop sending 'also' for section tabs: in storeTabs() keep 'also' only on the Home tab (HOME_PATHS) and give each section tab its section key instead ('section: s.key'). Give each entry of storeAreas() the same key ('section: s.key'; the Home entry gets 'home'). Do not change storeSections(), the labels, the order, 'exact', 'badge', 'foot' or 'advanced'. Step 0.17 (a dependency) adds storeNav(base, flags, canOpen?, counts) returning { tabs, areas } from one call of storeSections(); make the change wherever the tab and area objects are built (inside storeNav(), and in storeTabs()/storeAreas() if they still build their own), so storeNav()'s tabs and areas carry it too.

Today useIsCurrent() (line 40; line 43 tests item.also) is called by components that receive only the tabs, never the areas: StoreTabs (line 124), StoreSidebar (line 178, drawn with the tabs at line 117 of this file and at src/components/admin/admin-frame.tsx line 141) and AdminRail (src/components/admin/admin-rail.tsx line 35). AdminFrame (src/components/admin/admin-frame.tsx) is a server component, so filling 'also' back in there would send it again: the lookup must happen in the browser. Exactly: add `section?: string` to the types NavItem (line 19) and NavArea (line 50). Change `export function useIsCurrent()` to `export function useIsCurrent(areas: NavArea[] = [])`, and inside it, for an item that has `section` and no `also`, use `areas.find((a) => a.section === item.section)?.prefixes ?? []` where it reads `item.also ?? []` today (both branches of line 43). Add an optional prop `areas?: NavArea[]` to StoreTabs, StoreSidebar and AdminRail and pass it to their useIsCurrent(areas). In admin-frame.tsx pass `areas={areas ?? []}` to the StoreSidebar at line 141, the AdminRail at line 182 and the StoreTabs at line 228; in this file pass the component's own `areas` to the StoreSidebar at line 117. The platform's and the owner's layouts still send 'also' on their tabs, so they behave as today. The active tab, the sidebar and the phone menu must mark the same items as before for every address.

Update the expected shape of storeTabs() (no 'also' on section tabs, a 'section' key). Add one test: for a store with every feature on, JSON.stringify({ tabs: storeTabs(base, flags), areas: storeAreas(base, flags) }).length is under 14,000 characters, and every address under the base appears in it at most twice (once as an item's href, once as a prefix).

Run it; if it fails on the tab shape (an 'also' it expects on a section tab), update that expectation to the 'section' key; if it passes, leave the file unchanged. Do not change what it asserts about which tab is active.

commits.title: A save no longer carries the words: keep the way that measured better

changes.how: Way B, try first: a save that answers without drawing the route again. The Next guide (server-actions.md, 'A single response carries data and UI') says the response carries a re-render when the action calls updateTag, revalidatePath, refresh, sets a cookie or redirects. saveStorePageAction calls pagesChanged() (updateTag(pagesTag(...)) at about line 61). The editor already takes the saved page from the action's return value (onSaved in page-editor.tsx), so it does not need the redraw. Try, for the save action only: revalidateTag(pagesTag(member.store.id), { expire: 0 }) in place of updateTag, and measure whether the response still carries the route (the guide says only a stale-while-revalidate profile skips it; { expire: 0 } is not documented either way, so the measurement decides). The storefront must show a published change on its very next request: prove it with an int or e2e test that saves and then reads the public page. Never use the 'max' profile for a publish: the next visitor would get the old page. If { expire: 0 } still redraws, way B is not available for this action: go to way A. Apply the same to the platform's save in src/app/admin/(gated)/platform/pages/actions.ts and the sandbox's in src/app/admin/try/[sandbox]/actions.ts, and to the product save in src/app/admin/(gated)/[store]/products/actions.ts (updateTag(catalogTag) at about line 74), but only where the screen takes everything it shows after a save from the action's own answer; if a screen relies on the redraw (a list, a status line drawn by the server), return that value from the action first.

Way A, if way B does not reach the figure: the two big areas as client modules the browser keeps. A 'use client' file that imports builderEn and blocksEn and exports EditorWordsEn({ children }) drawing <AdminTextScope texts={{ builder: builderEn, blocks: blocksEn }}>{children}</AdminTextScope>. A twin editor-words-nb.tsx for Norwegian. The server editor views (src/app/admin/(gated)/[store]/pages/editor-views.tsx, the platform's editor-views.tsx, src/app/admin/try/[sandbox]/editor.tsx) draw the one for the account's language around the editor and drop 'builder' and 'blocks' from their adminTexts() lists. The words then travel as a content-hashed script, and a redraw sends only a reference. Keep it only if a build shows all three: one language's chunk in the page's script tags, not both; e2e/signed-in/content-types.spec.ts passes (the early Save of 31 October 2026); and the builder's first-scripts budget rises by no more than the bytes that left the document. It needs a named exception in src/components/admin/admin-catalogues.scan.test.ts and in the catalogue rule of src/components/admin/admin-bundle.scan.test.ts (these two files, and nothing else).
